name: Hot salt-water sitz bath after birth
what_people_do: Sit in a bowl or bath of hot water (sometimes with salt) in the first days and weeks after delivery.
why_they_say_it_works: To speed healing of tears and stitches, help the womb drain and "tighten" the vagina.

documented_by.source: Ekanem AD et al 2004, Trop Doct, PMID 15117138
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Calabar, 300 women: 70.7% sat in hot water (sitz bath) to aid perineal wound healing and improve vaginal tone.

documented_by.source: Okeke T et al 2013, Ann Med Health Sci Res, PMID 23634329
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Enugu, 420 mothers: 75% sat in hot salt water solution to aid lochia drainage and perineal healing.

documented_by.source: Udigwe GO, Emelumadu OF, Udigwe IB 2013, West Afr J Med, PMID 24488282
documented_by.quote_or_summary: Nnewi: 69.7% regularly did hot-water sitz baths.

evidence.finding: A 2024 Cureus trial combines far infrared and sitz bath after episiotomy (PMID 39310654); I saw the title only, abstract not read, UNVERIFIED. No trial of hot salt sitz bath alone was read.

source.name: agent4-traditional-practices.md, 12 Nov 2026 (research file in this project)

harm_note: Warm (not scalding) sitz baths are standard postnatal advice in many places; I did not open guidance, so this is UNVERIFIED as clinical guidance.
gaps: Guidance (NHS, WHO) on sitz baths not opened.
